Your win condition is a building, and it’s placed behind your side of the arena. That way, your opponent’s towers can’t touch yours, and you can damage their towers from a safe distance. The buildings you can use for this are Mortar and X-Bow. sources: Tower Troops are troops that defend the Crown Towers. The player can choose their Tower Troop before going into battle. Just like troop, spell and building cards, Tower Troop cards have rarities, and can be upgraded to a maximum level of 16, however, it cannot be upgraded past the player's King's Tower level even if it's under the starting level. The player can get Tower Troop cards through Lucky Chests or offers from the Shop. When upgrading to a new King Level, the player will get enough cards and gold to upgrade their Tower Princess. General information Each player has a pair of 3×3 size Crown Towers on their respective side of the Arena, one on the left and one on the right of the King's Tower. The Crown Towers are classified as a building and will be targeted by building-targeting troops. Destroying an opposing Crown Tower awards a player a Crown and grants the player additional territory across the river (commonly called a “pocket”) where cards can be cast upon (the Royal Recruits card needs both Crown Towers to be destroyed to be deployed in the pocket) There are certain cards that will deal reduced damage to Crown Towers. Source [3] covers deck management, card placement territory, emote communication, and elixir management principles.
sources: --- ## Combat & Damage Rules * **Targeting & Sight Range:** Troops automatically lock onto and engage the nearest valid target within their sight range. If no targets are nearby, troops advance toward the nearest enemy Crown Tower. * **Buildings:** Stationary structures with a decaying lifetime bar. They continuously lose hitpoints over time even if unattacked. * **Damage Types:** * **Point Damage:** Single-target damage. * **Area Damage (AoE):** Damages multiple targets within a radius simultaneously. * **Chain Damage:** Hits a primary target and bounces to adjacent targets. * **Friendly Fire & Buffs:** * Spells and negative effects (freeze, slow, pushback) **do not damage or affect friendly units**. * Positive effects (Rage, Heal, Clone) **only apply to friendly units**. (chunk how_to_play.md#5)

listed below do not use player's battle decks, Cards under Tournament Standard (Level 11) are adjusted up to this level, players can use Cards they have not unlocked yet, and all Cards are also adjusted to Tournament Standard if played in Party mode. Draft Challenge: A challenge in which before the match starts, players are given a choice between two Cards. The player gets to pick one while the other one is given to the opponent. This is repeated until one half of the player's deck is filled by Cards of the player's choice and the other half is filled by those given by the opponent. The player cannot see which Cards the opponent has taken or given to the player until the match starts. If a card is featured, one of the players will be guaranteed to get that card. Mirror and Clone are not available in this game mode. Triple Draft Challenge: Each player will pick one out of three cards eight times, with the other two cards (of each set) being discarded. The player will also be able to see what three cards their opponent can pick from, and vice versa. However, neither player can know what (chunk GameModes.txt#16)

**Deck & Hand:** Players battle using a deck of **8 Cards**. * **Territory:** * Cards are placed on the player's side of the arena (the non-red area ending at the river/bridge). * Most Spells and select cards (e.g., Miner, Goblin Barrel) can be placed anywhere on the field. * **Captured Territory:** Destroying an enemy Crown Tower expands the player's deployable territory slightly past the bridge on that side. *(Note: Royal Recruits require both opposing towers to be destroyed before they can be placed on the opponent's side).* * **Emotes:** Players can communicate using animated Emotes or quick text messages ("Thanks!", "Good Game!"). Emotes can be muted using the speech bubble toggle menu. --- ## Elixir Management **Elixir** is the resource required to play cards. It regenerates automatically over the course of the match. * **Elixir Advantage:** Occurs when a player has more available Elixir than their opponent. * **Positive Elixir Trade:** Defending an opponent's attack using less Elixir than the opponent spent to launch it. * **Defensive Advantage:** Crown Towers assist in defense for free, giving defenders an inherent Elixir efficiency advantage. To overcome this, attackers must construct large pushes or capitalize on when the opponent is out of counter-cards. (chunk how_to_play.md#2)

sources: Duel: Each player uses multiple Decks in a Best of 1 format. Before the battle starts, the player can see the opponent's 4 Decks and ban 2 of them. After that, they can choose to use one of the two decks that the opponent did not ban. Restricted Card Challenge: A challenge in which players get to build a deck restricted to certain subsets of cards in the game, for example: Retro Royale Challenge: A challenge in which players build decks exclusively with cards that were available before a certain date. Modern Royale Challenge: A challenge in which players build decks exclusively with cards released after a certain date. Arena Challenge: A challenge in which players build decks exclusively with cards unlocked at or below a certain Arena. Note that at the highest Arena, this becomes a Default Challenge: players use own decks. (Special Theme Challenge): A challenge in which players build decks exclusively with cards of certain theme(s). Modes listed below do not use player's battle decks, Cards under Tournament Standard (Level 11) are adjusted up to this level, players can use Cards they have not unlocked yet, and all Cards are also adjusted to Tournament Standard if played (chunk GameModes.txt#15)

a deck, but they can only occupy the Heroic or Wild Card slots. * **Saved Decks:** Players can save up to **3 decks** initially, expanding up to **5 decks** at Level 7 and **10 decks** at Level 17. --- ## Card Rotation & Cycling 1. **Starting Hand:** At the start of a match, 4 cards are randomly drawn into the hand, with a 5th card placed in the **"Next"** queue. * *Exceptions:* **Elixir Collector** and **Mirror** will never appear in the initial starting hand. 2. **Card Replacement Cooldown:** Playing a card moves the "Next" card into the hand with a **2-second delay** (reduced to 1 second during Double Elixir). 3. **Cycle Rule:** Once a card is played, it requires playing **3 other cards** before it reappears in the hand rotation. 4. **Evolutions:** Evolving cards require playing their standard version a set number of times (cycles) before triggering the Evolved form. *(Mirroring a card does not count toward Evolution cycle progression).* --- ## Combat & Damage Rules * **Targeting & Sight Range:** Troops automatically lock onto and engage the nearest valid target within their sight range. If no targets are nearby, troops advance toward the nearest enemy Crown Tower. * **Buildings:** (chunk how_to_play.md#4)

query: MATCH (d:DeckType)-[r:INCLUDES_CARD]->(c:Card) WITH c, collect(d.name) AS deck_types, collect(r.chunks) AS chunk_evidence WHERE size(deck_types) > 1 RETURN c.name AS card, deck_types, chunk_evidence
